The '''2004–2005 South African Premiership''', known as the '''Castle Premiership''' for sponsorship purposes, and also commonly referred to as the [[Premier Soccer League|PSL]] after the governing body, was the ninth season of the [[South African Premiership|Premiership]] since its establishment in 1996.  It was won by [[Kaizer Chiefs]], who defeated [[Bloemfontein Celtic F.C.|Bloemfontein Celtic]] on the last day of the season to retain the title.<ref>{{Cite web |title=A decade of success for Chiefs |url=https://www.kaizerchiefs.com/news/a-decade-of-success-for-chiefs/ |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=www.kaizerchiefs.com |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=South Africa 2004/05 |url=https://www.rsssf.org/tablesz/zaf05.html |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=www.rsssf.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Reporter |date=2005-05-23 |title=Chiefs defend PSL title |url=https://mg.co.za/article/2005-05-23-chiefs-defend-psl-title/ |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=The Mail & Guardian |language=en-ZA}}</ref>

[[Bidvest Wits|Wits]] were relegated for the first time in their history.<ref>{{Cite web |author=Staff Reporter |date=2005-05-27 |title=Wits tripped |url=https://mg.co.za/article/2005-05-27-wits-tripped/ |access-date=2025-01-01 |website=The Mail & Guardian |language=en-ZA}}</ref>
